subject: thermometer fever
title: What If 98.6 Stopped Being Normal? Human Bodies Have Been Cooling for 150 Years

scenes.text: What if normal body temperature wasn't 37 degrees any more? Yours probably isn't.
The number comes from 1851, when a German doctor measured 25,000 patients in Leipzig and settled on 37 Celsius, 98.6 Fahrenheit.
In 2020, Stanford researchers compared 677,000 temperature readings, from Civil War veterans in the 1860s to patients in the 2010s.
Every decade, Americans had cooled by about 0.03 degrees. Men born in the 1990s run about 0.6 degrees cooler than men born in the early 1800s.
Why? Probably less inflammation: fewer chronic infections, cleaner water, better dentistry, and homes that are heated and cooled.
Your body has less to fight, so it burns cooler. The textbook number is a measurement of people who no longer exist.

description:
What if 37 degrees Celsius was no longer the normal human body temperature? A 2020 Stanford study in eLife compared 677,423 readings from US Civil War veterans, a 1970s national survey and Stanford patients from 2007 to 2017.
It found body temperature falling by about 0.03 degrees Celsius per decade of birth: men born in the early 1990s run about 0.59 degrees cooler than men born in the early 1800s, and women about 0.32 degrees cooler than those born in the 1890s. The 37 degree standard came from Carl Wunderlich's 25,000 patients in Leipzig in 1851. Researchers suspect lower inflammation and climate-controlled homes.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Women cooled too, by about 0.32 degrees since the 1890s. What does your thermometer usually say, and what should we run through next?
